summary: CBDR and Asian range boxes, CBDR deviations, London protraction markers and profile labels, with a session statistics table.
overview: This community script follows ICT's London protraction idea for FX. It boxes the Central Bank Dealers Range (CBDR, 14:00 to 20:00 New York) and the Asian Range (20:00 to 00:00), labels their size in pips, and marks each range as valid or invalid against size limits.

It then projects CBDR standard deviations above and below, watches the protraction window (00:00 to 02:00) and the London session (02:00 to 05:00), and marks protraction highs or lows with short level lines and signal text. A statistics table counts how sessions played out, and a panel shows the timeframe and symbol.
how: The ideal CBDR is below 40 pips and the ideal Asian Range between 20 and 30 pips by default; ranges outside these limits are marked invalid. Up to three CBDR deviations can be drawn.

A protraction is confirmed when its extreme holds for a set number of bars (2 by default) and price closes back inside the range. Each day is assigned a profile, such as normal or negated, based on when the protraction printed.
Colors can adapt to a light or dark chart background.
use: Use the range boxes to see whether the day's setup meets the size rules.
Some traders watch the deviation lines as possible areas for the London move to reach.
Use the statistics table to review how often each profile appeared on past sessions.
Compare the protraction marker time with the normal window.
alerts: Alerts: members can create an alert on its conditions (for example "Profile Assigned", "Protraction", "Confirmed Protraction", "No Protraction") from the chart's alert dialog; alerts from indicators run while ZoroCharts is open in the browser.
notes: Made for FX pairs; ranges are measured in pips.
All times are New York time.
Five past sessions stay on the chart by default; the statistics count every session loaded.
